title: Temple of Saturn
visualBrief: Present-day Temple of Saturn ruin in the Roman Forum: eight mapped smooth granite columns, six across the northeast front and two short returns, Ionic capitals, surviving U-shaped entablature with inscribed front frieze, broken upper pediment core, occupied stone/concrete podium and specifically mapped low masonry. The missing roof, cella and remainder of the original temple are not reconstructed; independent Forum monuments remain native.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q746721/relation1849835 identifies this ruin. The current standard map provides eight individual column centres and five podium/fragment footprints inside the temple outline. Six columns form the northeast front; one return stands behind each end. Ordinary front and reverse photographs establish the inscription faces northeast, resolving the unsigned old rectangle axis. Raw east/south control vertices remain unchanged.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Map footprints control the approximately27×39m surviving podium envelope and nineteen-metre front column span. Ordinary photographs guide a4.1m podium mass, smooth tapered granite shafts,14.7m shaft top,15.45m Ionic capital top and17.5m entablature top above the lower base datum. The irregular pediment core rises to19m. These visualization dimensions, chamber niches and damage are estimates, not a survey or a historical reconstruction.

inscription.basis: The public-domain restoration text is original simplified recessed block geometry. Recess backs reuse the common granite graph to distinguish the carving under the engine lighting; exact serif shapes, stone color, damage and spacing remain approximate. No unique lettering texture is used. Lettering is centered on the beam and reads left-to-right when viewed from the northeast; the first draft was mirrored and was corrected from the current render.

This represents the surviving Roman Forum ruin, with eight smooth granite columns and Ionic capitals. The vanished roof and cella remain absent; recessed block lettering and chamber niches are approximate. Fine carvings, exact damage patterns, buried chambers and adjoining Forum ruins are outside scope. Current review status is recorded in qa.json.
